(-23) AMERICAN AIRLINES FLIGHT 1033, N412AA, AN MD-80 WS IN POSITION TO BEGIN TAKEOFF AT SYR ON MONDAY, FEBRUARY 21, 2000 WHEN SMOKE WAS DETECTED IN THE MAIN CABIN.  THE 133 PASSENERS WERE DEPLANED THROUGH THE VENTRAL EXIT ONTO THE RUNWAY WITH NO INJURIES.  AARF RESPONDED AND FOUND THE SOURCE OF THE SMOKE TO BE IN THE OVERHEAD BAGGAGE STORAGE BIN AT ROW 21 DEF. THE MECHANIC REMOVED THE MODULE AND BATTERY, PULLED THE APPLICABLE CIRCUIT BREAKERS, AND PREPARED THE AIRCRAFT FOR A FERRY FLIGHT TO ORD; ALL IN ACCORDANCE WITH INSTRUCTIONS FROM TULSA MAINTENANCE CONTROL.  THE AREA WAS INSPECTED FOR FIRE AND HEAT DAMAGE AND NONE WAS FOUND.  COMPANY MAINTENANCE REPLACED THE BATTERY AND CHARGER AND RETURNED THE AIRCRAFT TO SERVICE.  THIS INCIDENT IS CONSIDERED CLOSED.

(-23)WHILE TAXIING OUT FOR DEPARTURE, AT 1628 LT, THE COCKPIT AND CABIN FILLED UP WITH SMOKE. THE CAPTAIN STOPPED O

(-23)WHILE TAXIING OUT FOR DEPARTURE, AT 1628 LT, THE COCKPIT AND CABIN FILLED UP WITH SMOKE. THE CAPTAIN STOPPED ON TAXIWAY "C", SHUT DOWN THE ENGINES AND ALL ELECTRICAL POWER, AND ORDERED AN EVACUATION THROUGH THE MAIN CABIN DOOR AND ASSOCIATED AIRSTAIRS.  ONE PASSENGER REQUIRED OXYGEN, BUT WAS SOON RELEASED.  THERE WERE NO OTHER INJURIES.  THERE WAS NO FIRE, AND THE SMOKE STOPPED AS SOON AS THE AIRCRAFT WAS SHUT DOWN.  LOCAL CONTRACT MAINTENANCE (PIEDMONT/HAWTHORNE AVIATION) DETERMINED THAT THE SMOKE HAD BEEN CAUSED BY OIL CONTAMINATED APU BLEED AIR DUCTS.  THE APU WAS DEFEERED INOPERATIVE, IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE MEL.  A THOROUGH RUN OF BOTH ENGINES, WITH THE BLEEDS EXERCISED FULL RANGE, PRODUCED NO ADDITIONAL SMOKE, FUMES OR SMELLS.  THE AIRCRAFT LEFT THE NEXT MORNING, ON A REVENUE FLIGHT, WITH NO FURTHER PROBLEMS BEING REPORTED.  AS REPORTED BY THE DFW CMO, COMPANY MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL DETERMINED THAT THE SOURCE OF THE SMOKE WAS DEICING FLUID CONTAMINATION OF THE APU BLEED AIR SYSTEM, PROBABLY CAUSED BY THE SPRAYING OF DEICING FLUID DIRECTLY INTO THE APU INTAKE.

(-23) ON JANUARY 19, 2005, U.S. AIRWAYS EXPRESS (OPERATED BY MESA AIRLINES), FLIGHT 2814 RETURNED TO LEXINGTON, KY

(-23) ON JANUARY 19, 2005, U.S. AIRWAYS EXPRESS (OPERATED BY MESA AIRLINES), FLIGHT 2814 RETURNED TO LEXINGTON, KY (LEX) DUE TO SMOKE IN THE COCKPIT. FLIGHT 2814 DEPARTED LEXINGTON, KY (LEX) ENROUTE TO CHARLOTTE, NC. APPROXIMATELY 20 MINUTES INTO THE FLIGHT A FLIGHT ATTENDANT INFORMED THE CREW OF A HAZE AND ODOROUS SMELL IN THE AIRCRAFT. THE AIRCRAFT WAS FERRIED ON A NON-REVENUE FLIGHT TO CHARLOTTE MAINTENANCE FOR FURTHER INSPECTION. UPON ARRIVAL AT CHARLOTTE MAINTENANCE REPLACED THE NUMBER 2 AIR CONDITIONING PACK.

(-23) PASSENGER ^PRIVACY DATA OMITT^ ACCUSED OF RINGING HIS CALL BUTTON EXCESSIVELY THEREBY INTERFERING WITH THE FLIGHT ATTENDANTS DUTIES, FAR 121.580. THIS INCIDENT IS NOT IN ANY VIOLATION OF ANY SPECIFIC REGULATORY COMPLIANCE. IN CAPTAIN ^PRIVACY D^ NARRATIVE THE PASSENGER ^PRIVACY DATA OMITT^ WAS NOT INDICATED AS BEING DRUNK OR ABUSIVE OR DISORDERLY. IN CAPTAIN ^PRIVACY D^ NARRATIVE ^PRIVACY DAT^ APPEARS TO BE DISSATISFIED WITH THE SERVICE. ^PRIVACY DAT^ DID NOT VIOLATE ANY SPECIFIC REGULATION BY RINGING HIS CALL BUTTON EXCESSIVELY, THERBY INTERFERING WITH THE FLIGHT ATTENDANTS ABILITY TO PERFORM THEIR DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES. PART OF A FLIGHT ATTENDANTS DUTY IS TO ANSWER THE CALL BUTTON. WHAT IS EXCESSIVELY IS A MATTER OF OPTION, NOT A REGULATORY STANDARD. THIS INCIDENT IS AN AIR CARRIER CUSTOMER RELATION PROBLEM NOT A FAR VIOLATION. INJURY SUMMARY NOT KNOWN BY ASI.

THE AIRCRAFT DIVERTED TO ORF AND LANDED UNEVENTFULLY ON RUNWAY 23 AND TAXIED TO THE GATE. AN ON-CALL MECHANIC QUESTIONED THE FLIGHT ATTENDANTS AND LEARNED THAT THERE WAS NOT ANY VISIBLE SMOKE, ONLY HOT FUMES FROM AN OVERHEATED OVEN. THERE WAS NOT ANY FOOD PRODUCT IN THE OVEN AT THE TIME THE FUMES WERE NOTICED BY THE FLIGHT ATTENDANT. THE MECHANIC PERFORMED AN INSPECTION AND OPERATED THE VARIOUS SYSTEMS ON THE AIRCRAFT. ONE FLIGHT ATTENDANT WAS SHAKEN UP BUT NOT INJURED AND REMAINED AT ORF. A REPLACEMENT FLIGHT ATTENDANT WAS FLOWN IN. THE OVEN WAS DEFERRED PER THE MINIMUM EQUIPMENT LIST, AND ALL BUT 2 PASSENGERS REBOARDED FOR THE CONTINUATION FLIGHT TO TPA.

HIS INJURIES CONSISTED OF A CUT ON THE HEAD (NO STITCHES REQUIRED), A BLACK AND BLUE TOE ON HIS RIGHT FOOT AND AN INJURED THUMB. ALTHOUGH HE RECEIVED A CT SCAN AND X-RAYS, HIS INJURIES WERE MINOR AND REQUIRED ONLY FIRST AID LEVEL TREATMENT.

(-23) NWA FLIGHT #1749 DEPARTED KMSP ENROUTE TO MMCZ. SHORTLY AFTER LEVEL OFF THE FIRST OFFICER NOTICED A FUEL IMBA

(-23) NWA FLIGHT #1749 DEPARTED KMSP ENROUTE TO MMCZ. SHORTLY AFTER LEVEL OFF THE FIRST OFFICER NOTICED A FUEL IMBALANCE GREATER THAN THAT ALLOWABLE. THE AMOUNT OF FUEL USED (TOTAL FUEL LOADED MINUS FUEL ONBOARD) AND THE FUEL BURN NUMBERS WERE CORRECT, HOWEVER IT APPEARED ALL OF THE FUEL, FOR BOTH ENGINES WAS BEING BURNED OUT OF THE RIGHT MAIN FUEL TANK. AFTER DISCUSSION WITH DISPATCH AND MTC, THE DECISION WAS MADE TO DIVERT TO KMEM. IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE FUELER IN KMSP HAD LEFT THE MODE SELECT SWITCH ON THE REFUELING CONTROL PANEL IN THE REFUEL POSITION AND THE REFUELING VALVE FOR THE LEFT WING IN THE OPEN POSITION. ALSO, A RELAY, REMOVED AFTER THE EVENT, WAS DETERMINED TO HAVE FAILED IN SUCH A MANNER THAT NO ELECTRICAL POWER WAS AVAILABLE TO CLOSE THE TWO OPEN FUELING VALVES WHEN THE LANDING GEAR SELECTOR WAS RAISED. THE FAILED RELAY PREVENTED THE FLOW OF POWER TO THE SHUT SECTION OF THE TWO VALVES INVOLVED. THUS THE FUEL BOOST PUMP PRESSURE MOVED THE FUEL FROM THE CENTER/RIGHT WING TANK TO THE LEFT WING TANK.
